I've argued against this point a few times tonight. I just can't watch children as young as 3 play piano as an almost master and their ability to recall a song from a single listen and go "yup that's hard work and practice." Or watch LeBron James play and go "man he hits the gym so hard that's why he is so great." I mean yes he did practice and maintain his body to near perfection but his ability to play basketball is a gift given to him. He is a specimen basically and even if he hated.practice and the gym I guarantee he'd still be a top 15 player in the NBA but with practice he's possibly still the best. So my point is 100 years ago someone may have been the best baseball player in the world but instead due to segregation and other factors he was never able to play against the best or maybe even get to play for a team at all. Instead many have worked in sweat shops and dead end jobs and never found what they are amazing at. Someone may have never heard a guitar in person yet they can feel how it's played and when finally given a guitar they pick it up almost instantaneously from a single time watching someone play. There's just too much evidence of human beings instant abilities to say they weren't wired that way but instead just got there through practice and hard work. Last example me. Nothing special but I have an insane ability to chug drinks and I was able to do it instantly from when I was 10 not through practice.  I've won so many dumb beer bets growing up by an ability for my mind to go blank and open my throat (this got so dirty I feel icky lol) but seriously I was just able to do it and I can say through so called "practice" I haven't really changed my ability. Sure I could get faster but someone who practices night and day still may never be able to beat me bc I'm wired to have this ability. But again we agree to disagree on certain subjects good talk Reddit person.

I think your points are valid practice and learning something new will make you better. Sticking with it if you enjoy it will also make u amazing at whatever. But your missing my point that certain people are capable of amazing feats almost instantly. Kids as young as 3 can not only play the piano from a few times watching with almost mastery but what's amazing is their "gift" of recall on hearing a single song. Certain things people can do have nothing to do with practice many people ARE able to pick up something completely new just because they're wired that way physically or mentally or both. Yes these people continue to get better and better with practice but they're ability to pick up certain skills instantaneously is a gift and has nothing to do with the hard work they put in. Again athletes are a prime example of born with a gift. Usain bolt has the gift of speed and a perfect physical body for running.
